tuning-loop: judge searches, then measure a setting before adopting it.

A small corpus and some judged searches. kb config --set shows what a setting would do,
kb explain shows why a chunk ranks where it does, kb eval scores the log, --save-baseline
keeps that score, and --set ... --compare says whether another setting beats it. None of
this writes the config, and explain and eval never write the search log.

  $ kb init --model fake:8
  created location $WORK/proj/.kb
  created store "default" in $WORK/proj (model fake:8)

  $ kb add --dir $WORK/notes/deploy
  added data/deploy/README.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/backup.md
  added data/backup.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/tmux.md
  added data/tmux.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/oncall.md
  added data/oncall.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/cache.md
  added data/cache.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/flags.md
  added data/flags.md (2 chunks)

Tags match case-insensitively: --tag Docker finds an entry tagged docker.

  $ kb search "container image" --mode fts --tag Docker --caller claude
  search 1 · 2 hits
  [1] data/backup.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02
  Nightly backup › (intro)
  # Nightly backup

  The nightly backup writes a container image of the database to the archive volume.

  [2] data/tmux.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-03
  Tmux survives logout › (intro)
  # Tmux survives logout

  Detach tmux and the session survives logout. Run the container image of the shell tools inside it.
  search_id=1

  $ kb search "container image" --mode fts --tag docker --caller claude
  search 2 · 2 hits
  [1] data/backup.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02

  The nightly backup writes a container image of the database to the archive volume.

  # Tmux survives logout

  Detach tmux and the session survives logout. Run the container image of the shell tools inside it.
  search_id=2

Judge a few searches. Each query has a gold chunk marked useful.

  $ kb feedback --last 1 --useful --caller claude
  recorded: search 2 rank 1 useful=1 (newest search for claude, (time): "container image")

  $ kb search "nightly backup" --mode fts --caller claude
  search 3 · 2 hits
  [1] data/backup.md · updated 2026-02-02
  Nightly backup: How the nightly backup runs.

Settings and diagnostics. --set shows a result without writing it: the settings hash changes
with it, and the config file does not.

  $ kb config --json
  {
  ...
        "rrf_k": 60,
  ...
  ~   "settings_hash": "[0-9a-f]{64}"
  }

  $ kb config --set search.rrf_k=20 --json
  {
  ...
        "rrf_k": 20,
  ...
  ~   "settings_hash": "[0-9a-f]{64}"
  }

  $ grep rrf_k .kb/stores/default/config.toml
  [stderr] grep: no line of .kb/stores/default/config.toml matches rrf_k
  [exit 1]

explain shows every candidate and where its score comes from. It does not write the search log.

  $ kb explain "restart the service" --mode fts
  ~ explain "restart the service" · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  settings: rrf_k=60 fts_weight=1 vec_weight=1 bm25 text=1 heading=2 title=3 list_limit=20 candidate_limit=40 per_entry_cap=3 exact=1
  fts: match "restart" AND "the" AND "service" · AND
  tiers: phrase "restart the service" (2 rows) · near NEAR("restart" "the" "service", 8) (2 rows) · and "restart" AND "the" AND "service" (2 rows)
  lists: fts 2 rows · vec 0 rows · 2 candidates
  ...

  ~ #1  rrf [0-9.]+  data/deploy/README.md  \[returned as hit #1\]
  ...
      fts  rank 1  tier phrase  bm25 -4.1671  columns text -3.6318 · heading 0.0000 · title -2.3473
      vec  -
      rrf  fts 1/(60+1)=0.016393

  ~ #2  rrf [0-9.]+  data/deploy/README.md › \(intro\)  \[returned as hit #2\]
  ...
      fts  rank 2  tier phrase  bm25 -3.7992  columns text -3.3799 · heading 0.0000 · title -2.1107
      vec  -
      rrf  fts 1/(60+2)=0.016129

  $ kb explain "restart the service" --mode fts --json
  {
  ...
    "mode": "fts",
  ...
        "status": "returned",
  ...
  }

The next search id continues the sequence: config, explain and eval wrote nothing to the log.

  $ kb search "log in" --mode fts --caller claude
  search 8 · 1 hit
  [1] data/tmux.md · updated 2026-02-03
  Tmux survives logout: Keep sessions alive after you log out.
  search_id=8

Score the log. Every judged query has its gold at rank 1, so the scores are perfect; the
sample is small and the report says so.

  $ kb eval --mode fts
  ~ eval · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  searches: 8 logged · 6 useful · 0 --none · 0 not-useful only · 2 unjudged · 0 with opens
  queries=6 hit@8=1.000 [1.000, 1.000] mrr=1.000 [1.000, 1.000] ndcg@8=1.000 [1.000, 1.000]
  entry: queries=6 hit@8=1.000 [1.000, 1.000] mrr=1.000 [1.000, 1.000] ndcg@8=1.000 [1.000, 1.000]
  gold not in index: 0 chunks (0 queries dropped) · 0 entries · 0 opens
  negatives in top 8: 0
  intervals: 95% bootstrap, 1000 resamples, seed 1
  small sample: differences under ±CI are noise (6 queries < eval.min_judged 30)

  $ kb eval --mode fts --save-baseline
  ...
  ~ saved baseline "default" \(6 queries, settings [0-9a-f]{12}\) to \$WORK/proj/.kb/stores/default/eval/default\.json

  $ exists .kb/stores/default/eval/default.json

Try a setting against the baseline. Nothing changes order here, so every query ties.

  $ kb eval --mode fts --set search.bm25.title=5 --compare
  ~ compare · baseline "default" \(.*\)
  ~         now \(mode fts · settings [0-9a-f]{12} · fake:8 · 6 entries\) · k 8
  ...
    hit@8        1.000    1.000   +0.000  [+0.000, +0.000]  0/0/6     1.000
  ...
  ~ small sample: 6 paired queries < eval.min_judged 30; .*

Adopt a setting by writing it to the store's config, then search once more: the log now holds
two settings, and kb stats settings lists one row for each.

  $ write .kb/stores/default/config.toml @cfg
  $ kb search "log in" --mode fts --caller claude
  search 9 · 1 hit
  [1] data/tmux.md · updated 2026-02-03
  Tmux survives logout: Keep sessions alive after you log out.
  search_id=9

  $ kb stats settings --json
  {
  ...
  ~ \s+"searches": 1,
  ...
  ~ \s+"searches": 8,
  ...
    "searches_loaded": 9,
  ...
  }

-- @cfg --
version = 1

[embed]
model = "fake:8"

[[sources]]
path = "data"
layout = "entries"

[search]
rrf_k = 20
